name: wien-filter
description: Closed form: x(t) = v_d t + ((v0 - v_d)/w) sin(w t), solved for x = L. Crossed fields - 50 kV/m along +y and 0.5 T along +z - pass an ion moving along +x at v_d = E/B = 100 km/s undeflected, whatever its mass. This one is 20% too fast (m/z 100 accelerated through 7462.274 V, so v0 = 120 km/s): the magnetic push q v B outweighs the electric one q E, and the ion gyrates at w = |q| B / m about the E x B drift, arriving at the plane x = 50 mm after 0.4171350 us, 0.837 mm toward -y. With B ignored the electric field is transverse, x advances at v0, and the ion arrives at L / v0 = 0.4166667 us - 0.11% early, eleven hundred times the tolerance. The expectation is a root of the closed-form trajectory, found by Newton's method outside this engine. B is declared in gauss (5000 G) to exercise the unit.
